d390_boost.about: The RenderThread's boost with compose-rs's own hint session (D390, holding the main thread too since D440, reporting both threads' CPU time against 8.33 ms since D500), computed from this run's traces: per run (scenario-app-run), the boost picture of HWUI's counter alone (hwui_min, as render_boost), of compose-rs's session's minimum (app_min), and of the higher of both sessions' active CPU votes (effective_votes: what the power HAL applies), plus CPU time and work by thread kind over the measured window (13 s scrolling, 9 s animating), for scroll, animation, stress_scroll and stress_animation.

prefetch_slices.about: Item composition and prefetch work on the main thread, computed from this run's scroll and stress_scroll traces: per run (scenario-app-run), for each slice name (compose-rs's prefetch sections and frame phases; Compose's lazy prefetch and recomposition sections), the number of slices from the stats' start, their wall time, the main thread's running time inside them, its work (ms on the fastest core at its highest frequency, as work_ms) and its running time on the little cores. Round 11's are in results/2026-10-23-pixel-8-pro-round-11.json.

lazy_lists.about: compose-rs's lazy lists in this run's traces (D470-D496: only the items in view placed, prefetch from the first layout). runs: per scroll and stress_scroll run, from the stats' start, the count and total wall time (ms) of in-frame rounds (`compose-rs: recompose and layout again`), the frames holding one, text layouts inside a `compose-rs: frame` (text_layouts_in_frames), prefetch compositions and measurements, draw-ahead steps, compose-rs frames and replays. first_frame: per traced start (feed, big, stress), the sections inside the first `compose-rs: frame` (count, total ms).

late_do_frames.about: doFrames starting more than 2 ms after their vsync (measure.py's late_do_frames), for both apps, per run (scenario-app-run) of scroll, animation, stress_scroll and stress_animation, from the stats' start: do_frames (all doFrames), and per late doFrame its lateness (from the expected timeline's start), its duration, the main thread's runnable (R, R+) and running time between the vsync and the doFrame (the rest: sleeping, woken late), FrameTimeline's jank and present types for its vsync, on_time_finish, and margin_ms (the expected deadline less the frame's actual end). summary: counts (over 4 and 6 ms late, mostly runnable, mostly running, janky other than buffer stuffing, presented late, finished late) and the margins' minimum and median.
